html:
The Klamath are a Native people of the Klamath Basin in south central Oregon, around Upper Klamath Lake and the marshes of the Williamson and Sprague rivers.

They gathered the seeds of the yellow pond lily, called wocas, fished for suckers and salmon, and hunted waterfowl in the marshes. Their language is related to that of the Modoc to the south. In 1864 the Klamath, the Modoc and the Yahooskin band of Northern Paiute signed a treaty creating the Klamath Reservation; quarrels there led part of the Modoc to break away and fight the Modoc War of 1872 and 1873.

In 1954 the United States ended its recognition of the Klamath Tribes under the termination policy and sold most of their forest. Recognition was restored in 1986. In 2023 and 2024 four dams on the Klamath River were removed, the largest dam removal in history, to let salmon return. Neighbours include the Achumawi and the Shasta.
sum: The Klamath are a Native people of the Klamath Basin in south central Oregon, around Upper Klamath Lake and the marshes of the Williamson and Sprague rivers.
